title: Andrii Yermak

fields.label: Position held
fields.value: Head of the Office of the President of Ukraine

summary: Andriy Borysovych Yermak is a Ukrainian politician and former film producer who served as the head of the Office of the President of Ukraine from 2020 to 2025, playing a significant role in the country's political landscape during a critical period of conflict and reform.

sections.heading: Early Life and Education
paragraphs: Andriy Yermak was born on 21 November 1971 in [[kyiv|Kyiv]], [[ukraine|Ukraine]], which was then part of [[soviet-union|the Soviet Union]]. His mother, Maria, is Russian, while his father, Borys, is Jewish and a native of Kyiv. The couple married in 1971, and Yermak has a younger brother named Denys.

In 1995, Yermak graduated from the Institute of International Relations at [[taras-shevchenko|Taras Shevchenko]] National University in Kyiv with a master's degree in international private law. He obtained his law practice license the same year.

sections.heading: Career in Law and Media
paragraphs: Following his graduation, Yermak began working for the 'Proxen' law firm at the request of a professor. In 1997, he established his own law firm, focusing on intellectual property and commercial law, and became a member of the Association of Lawyers of Ukraine.

Yermak also ventured into media, founding the Garnet International Media Group in 2012 and producing films such as 'Rules of the Fight' and 'The Line.' He is a member of both the [[ukrainian|Ukrainian]] Film Academy and the European Film Academy since 2017.

sections.heading: Political Involvement
paragraphs: Yermak became acquainted with [[volodymyr-zelenskyy|Volodymyr Zelenskyy]] in 2011 and later contributed to Zelenskyy's presidential campaign in 2019. On 21 May 2019, he was appointed as Presidential Aide for Foreign Policy Issues, where he played a key role in negotiating prisoner exchanges with Russia during the [[war-in-donbas|war in Donbas]].

On 11 February 2020, Yermak was appointed as the Head of the Office of the [[president-of-ukraine|President of Ukraine]], becoming a crucial advisor and member of the National Security and Defense Council the following day.

sections.heading: Influence and Controversies
paragraphs: As head of the presidential office, Yermak was seen as a significant power broker [[coal-in-ukraine|in Ukraine]], with Politico referring to him as Kyiv's 'Green Cardinal' in 2023. He was influential in military and foreign policy decisions, including advocating for the defense of [[bakhmut|Bakhmut]] in 2022.

However, his tenure was marked by controversies, including allegations of eroding democratic checks and balances and involvement in corruption scandals. Following a raid on his home by anti-corruption agents on 28 November 2025, Yermak resigned from his position, and he was formally removed from key government bodies by presidential decree on 6 December 2025.

sections.heading: Personal Life
paragraphs: Yermak has lived in Kyiv throughout his life. He is currently single and has no children.
